overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common spear phishing tactics such as targeted emails to high-level personnel, use of recently registered suspicious domains with privacy protection, SPF/DKIM passing but domain spoofing, malicious attachments with macros or exploits, URL obfuscation via chained subdomains, and detailed SMTP and WAF logs. The scenarios align well with known attack patterns and MITRE ATT&CK techniques, including behavioral analytics and sandbox detonation findings, which adds to their credibility.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset is consistent and adheres well to a clear schema. Each entry contains a scenario description, detailed technical data with email headers, body, SMTP logs, domain registration info, DNS resolution, webserver and WAF logs where applicable, IOC hashes, indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. The structure and field naming are uniform across samples. Some fields are null where not applicable, maintaining schema integrity.
suggestions: Include explicit fields for attachment file size and macro presence flags to facilitate automated parsing.
Provide full base64 data or a note indicating truncation to avoid ambiguity in attachment content representation.
Add timestamps in SMTP transaction logs in a consistent format to improve temporal correlation.
Consider including sender IP geolocation data to enrich domain registration country info.
Incorporate a field for email client or user agent details from headers or logs to enhance realism.
Standardize the format of URL obfuscation field to explicitly indicate the obfuscation technique used.
Add a unique identifier field per sample for easier referencing and tracking.
